channel.title: SymbiQ · The Ledger
channel.description: Every public, dated, falsifiable claim SymbiQ tracks about quantum computing, and every check-in, proposed verdict and resolution against it. Criteria are frozen before the deadline; misses are never deleted.

item.title: Check-in (no signal): NVIDIA's Jensen Huang said truly useful quantum computers are 15 to 30 years away, with 20 years as the figure “a whole bunch of us would believe.”
item.description: On 20 March 2025, at Nvidia's Quantum Day, Huang walked the remark back: "This is the first event in history where a company CEO invites all of the guests to explain why he was wrong" (CNBC). He named no revised range, so there is no new dated claim to track. This one stands as stated and resolves on its own criteria.

item.title: Check-in (no signal): IBM expects the first cases of verified quantum advantage to be confirmed by the wider community by the end of 2026.
item.description: On 30 July 2026 IBM and Qedma announced a quantum-advantage result on commercially available IBM hardware and released the circuits to the Quantum Advantage Tracker for classical benchmarking. That is the claimant's own announcement, so it is logged without a signal. The claim scores confirmation by the wider community, which had not been established when this entry was captured.

item.title: Check-in (at risk): Pasqal's roadmap pointed to 10,000 qubits in 2026.
item.description: Pasqal's own 2025 roadmap (12 June 2025) says it is "moving towards 10,000 qubits by 2028". The claimant has moved the date two years. The 2026 claim is still scored as it was made.

item.title: Check-in (at risk): QuNorth said Magne, the logical-qubit machine it is buying from Microsoft and Atom Computing, would be ready for its first tasks by the new year 2026/27.
item.description: On 2 September 2026 The Quantum Insider reported the building complete and installation only beginning, and that "MAGNE is expected to be fully operational in the spring of 2027". Full operation is a later bar than first tasks, so this is a warning, not a verdict. The archived copy was taken on 23 September 2026.

item.title: Check-in (off track): Rigetti's own roadmap commits to a 100+ qubit chiplet system in 2025, 150+ qubits in 2026, and 1,000+ qubits in 2027.
item.description: The 2025 interim target, a 100+ qubit chiplet-based system, slipped. On 9 January 2026 Rigetti said it was revising its roadmap and that its 108-qubit Cepheus-1-108Q was "now expected to reach general availability around the end of the first quarter of 2026". Under this claim's criteria an interim slip still leaves PARTIALLY_VERIFIED open if the 2027 target is substantially met.

item.title: Now tracking: The EU's NIS Cooperation Group set the end of 2026 for every Member State to have started a national post-quantum transition.
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-09-23. Resolves by 2026-12-31 (+90 day grace). Criteria: Resolves VERIFIED if, by 31 Dec 2026, all 27 Member States have initiated a national PQC transition strategy following the roadmap's First Steps, as reported by the NIS Cooperation Group, the European Commission or ENISA, or shown by each state's published plan. The grace period is 90 days because status reporting lags the deadline. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if a majority but not all have. NOT_VERIFIED if fewer than half have, or if no status is published by the end of the grace period.

item.title: Now tracking: Fujitsu and RIKEN scheduled the launch of a 1,000-qubit superconducting quantum computer for 2026.
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-09-23. Resolves by 2026-12-31 (+30 day grace). Criteria: Resolves VERIFIED if, by 31 Dec 2026 (plus grace), Fujitsu and/or RIKEN have launched a superconducting quantum computer with at least 1,000 physical qubits, announced as operational for research or customer use. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if the launch falls in Japan's fiscal year 2026 but after the calendar year (January to March 2027), or if a 1,000-qubit chip is shown but not launched as a working system. NOT_VERIFIED otherwise.

item.title: Now tracking: IBM will deliver Kookaburra, its first modular processor designed to store and process encoded information, in 2026.
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-09-23. Resolves by 2026-12-31 (+30 day grace). Criteria: Resolves VERIFIED if, by 31 Dec 2026 (plus grace), IBM has publicly demonstrated a Kookaburra processor module that both stores error-encoded information in its qLDPC memory and processes it with its attached logic unit, confirmed by an IBM announcement plus independent technical reporting or a paper. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if Kookaburra is shown but demonstrates only the encoded memory or only the logic, not both working together. NOT_VERIFIED if no Kookaburra module has been shown by the deadline.

item.title: Now tracking: IBM expects the first cases of verified quantum advantage to be confirmed by the wider community by the end of 2026.
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-09-23. Resolves by 2026-12-31 (+30 day grace). Criteria: IBM's own test is the one scored: confirmation by the wider community, not an IBM announcement. Resolves VERIFIED if, by 31 Dec 2026 (plus grace), at least one quantum-advantage result run on IBM hardware has been confirmed by a party that is neither IBM nor an author of the result: a peer-reviewed paper or an independent group stating that the best classical methods it tried cannot match the result, with no published classical reproduction of that result standing at the resolution date. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if a result is under open dispute at the deadline (classical work matches part of it but not all). NOT_VERIFIED if every claimed case has been matched classically, or no case has been confirmed outside IBM and its co-authors.

item.title: Now tracking: IonQ's roadmap puts 10,000 physical qubits on a single chip in 2027.
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-09-23. Resolves by 2027-12-31 (+30 day grace). Criteria: Resolves VERIFIED if, by 31 Dec 2027 (plus grace), IonQ has demonstrated a single chip with at least 10,000 physical qubits trapped, controlled and running gates, confirmed by IonQ plus independent reporting or a paper. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if the chip has 10,000 trap sites but fewer operate as qubits, or if 10,000 qubits are reached across more than one chip. NOT_VERIFIED otherwise.

item.title: Now tracking: NIST expects to finalise a standard for HQC, its backup post-quantum key-exchange algorithm, in 2027.
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-09-23. Resolves by 2027-12-31 (+30 day grace). Criteria: Resolves VERIFIED if, by 31 Dec 2027 (plus grace), NIST has published the final Federal Information Processing Standard for HQC (expected to be numbered FIPS 207). There is no partial outcome: a draft is not a standard. NOT_VERIFIED if only a draft exists by then.

item.title: Now tracking: Pasqal's roadmap pointed to 10,000 qubits in 2026.
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-09-23. Resolves by 2026-12-31 (+30 day grace). Criteria: Scored as made on 12 March 2024. A later roadmap from the claimant that moves the date does not void the claim; it is logged as a check-in. Resolves VERIFIED if, by 31 Dec 2026 (plus grace), Pasqal operates or delivers a neutral-atom system with at least 10,000 physical qubits usable for computation. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if at least 10,000 atoms are trapped and controlled in a demonstration but not in an operated or delivered system. NOT_VERIFIED otherwise.

item.title: Now tracking: PsiQuantum planned to have its utility-scale quantum computing site near Brisbane operational by the end of 2027.
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-09-23. Resolves by 2027-12-31 (+30 day grace). Criteria: "Operational" is read as the quantum computer on the site running computations, not the building being finished. Resolves VERIFIED if, by 31 Dec 2027 (plus grace), PsiQuantum's system at the Brisbane site is running computations, confirmed by PsiQuantum or the Australian or Queensland government plus independent reporting. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if the facility is complete and a smaller or partial system runs there. NOT_VERIFIED otherwise.

item.title: Now tracking: QuEra will introduce a quantum computer with 100 logical qubits and over 10,000 physical qubits in 2026.
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-09-23. Resolves by 2026-12-31 (+30 day grace). Criteria: Resolves VERIFIED if, by 31 Dec 2026 (plus grace), QuEra has introduced a system (available to customers or publicly operated) with at least 100 error-corrected logical qubits and more than 10,000 physical qubits, confirmed by a QuEra announcement plus independent reporting or a paper. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if only one of the two figures is met, or both are met only in a one-off research demonstration rather than an introduced system. NOT_VERIFIED otherwise.

item.title: Now tracking: QuNorth said Magne, the logical-qubit machine it is buying from Microsoft and Atom Computing, would be ready for its first tasks by the new year 2026/27.
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-09-23. Resolves by 2026-12-31 (+30 day grace). Criteria: Resolves VERIFIED if, by 31 Dec 2026 (plus grace), Magne is installed in Copenhagen and has run its first user or research workloads, reported by QuNorth, Microsoft or Atom Computing plus independent reporting. Commissioning and acceptance testing are not first tasks. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if the machine is installed and running acceptance tests but no workloads by the deadline. NOT_VERIFIED if it is not installed.

item.title: Resolved, Not verified: Atom Computing and Microsoft announced a commercial quantum machine with 24 entangled logical qubits, available for delivery in 2025.
item.description:
Evidence gathered from the pre-registered resolver sources only. The criteria required a commercial customer to have RECEIVED AND OPERATED a system matching the 24-entangled-logical-qubit specification by 31 Dec 2025 plus the 30-day grace (30 Jan 2026), and said in advance that an order or a demo does not count.
One commercial sale is identifiable in the named sources: QuNorth (Denmark, funded by EIFO and the Novo Nordisk Foundation), which contracted in 2025 for Magne — an Atom Computing / Microsoft system specified at roughly 50 logical qubits on about 1,225 physical neutral atoms, announced July 2025 with construction beginning that autumn. As of 2 September 2026, more than seven months after the grace period closed, The Quantum Insider reports that the building intended to house Magne has only just been completed, that installation is beginning, and that the system is expected to be fully operational in spring 2027.
So no system was operating at a customer site inside the window — not at the announced 24-logical specification, and not at the differently-specified 50-logical one. That also rules out PARTIALLY_VERIFIED, which required a differently-specified system to have shipped in the window; none did. The January 2025 HPCwire roll-out report logged at intake describes an offering being made available, not a delivery — exactly the distinction the criteria fixed in advance, which is the whole reason it was fixed in advance.
Nothing here is a judgement about intent. Hardware schedules slip, and the original announcement was explicit that delivery was a 2025 plan. What the Ledger records is that the dated, falsifiable version of the claim did not come true inside its own window.

item.title: Resolved, Not verified: IonQ targeted 99.999% (“five nines”) logical two-qubit gate fidelity by the end of 2025.
item.description:
Evidence gathered from the pre-registered resolver sources only. The tracked target, as stated in IonQ's July 2024 roadmap announcement, was 99.999% (“five nines”) LOGICAL two-qubit gate fidelity using small-distance quantum error-correcting codes, by the end of 2025.
Inside the window (31 Dec 2025 plus the 30-day grace, i.e. by 30 Jan 2026) IonQ did publish a two-qubit gate result: on 20–21 October 2025 it reported a gate error of 8.4(7)×10⁻⁵ — about 99.9916% fidelity — using Electronic Qubit Control without ground-state cooling, demonstrated on prototype systems in IonQ's R&D labs (arXiv:2510.17286; IonQ newsroom; The Quantum Insider, 21 Oct 2025). That is a PHYSICAL (native) gate fidelity. No error-correcting code is involved, and it is measured on prototype hardware rather than a deployed system. It is a real advance, it was reported as a world record on the physical axis, and it comfortably clears the same roadmap's separate >99.9% native target — but it is not the claim tracked here. No result at or above 99.999% logical two-qubit gate fidelity with small-distance QEC codes appears in any named resolver source inside the window.
On the PARTIALLY_VERIFIED branch, recorded so the reading is auditable rather than assumed: the criteria offer that branch for “a result close to but short of five nines (e.g. four nines) … reported as the headline achievement instead.” The desk reads it as scoped to LOGICAL fidelity, because the sentence immediately before it forbids conflating the native figure with the logical one. A four-nines PHYSICAL result is a different measurement, not a near miss on the same one, so the branch does not fire.
This is a statement about a dated claim and its deadline, not about the people who made it.

item.title: Check-in (off track): Atom Computing and Microsoft announced a commercial quantum machine with 24 entangled logical qubits, available for delivery in 2025.
item.description: Resolution pass run. The one identified commercial sale (QuNorth / Magne) had not been installed, let alone operated, by the 30 Jan 2026 grace deadline — as of 2 Sep 2026 the housing facility is only just finished and full operation is expected spring 2027. This supersedes the intake note's reading of the Jan 2025 HPCwire piece, which reported an offering, not a delivery. Moved to proposed with a drafted NOT_VERIFIED verdict; awaiting the second key.

item.title: Check-in (off track): IonQ targeted 99.999% (“five nines”) logical two-qubit gate fidelity by the end of 2025.
item.description: Resolution pass run. IonQ's in-window publication (20–21 Oct 2025) is a PHYSICAL two-qubit gate fidelity of ~99.9916% on prototype hardware, not the 99.999% LOGICAL figure with small-distance QEC codes that this claim tracks. Moved to proposed with a drafted NOT_VERIFIED verdict and full reasoning; awaiting the second key before it is published as resolved.

item.title: Check-in (on track): Atom Computing and Microsoft announced a commercial quantum machine with 24 entangled logical qubits, available for delivery in 2025.
item.description: A January 2025 report describes an on-premise system from the same Atom Computing/Microsoft partnership supporting up to 50 logical qubits -- more than this claim's own 24, which is why this is logged on_track rather than off_track. Not treated as a resolution: the desk still needs to confirm this is the SAME delivery the original claim described, not a different, larger, later system being counted as satisfying an earlier, smaller promise.

item.title: Check-in (no signal): NVIDIA's Jensen Huang said truly useful quantum computers are 15 to 30 years away, with 20 years as the figure “a whole bunch of us would believe.”
item.description: Captured at seed, 19 months after the remark. Real-world consequence worth noting for context (not evidence toward the verdict): the comment briefly wiped tens of billions of dollars off publicly traded quantum companies' market capitalisation the same week, and Huang has since visibly softened the framing at subsequent public appearances -- a check-in for the desk to track is whether he has ever named a revised range, which would be a genuine restatement worth logging as its own event.

item.title: Check-in (no signal): IBM will deliver a large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computer (“Starling”) by 2029, running 100 million quantum operations on 200 logical qubits.
item.description: Captured at seed. IBM Quantum Starling is IBM's stated terminal milestone on a roadmap with earlier named systems (Loon, Kookaburra, Cockatoo) due in the intervening years -- those intermediate milestones are the check-ins to watch for, not just the 2029 date.

item.title: Check-in (off track): IonQ targeted 99.999% (“five nines”) logical two-qubit gate fidelity by the end of 2025.
item.description: Deadline plus grace period has passed with no independent report found (during this session's research pass) of IonQ publishing a 99.999% logical two-qubit gate fidelity result. That absence of evidence is not itself a verdict -- it needs a deliberate resolution pass checking IonQ's own 2025 technical announcements and any arXiv papers before this can be marked NOT_VERIFIED rather than just resolvable.

item.title: Check-in (no signal): Microsoft says its Majorana 1 / Topological Core approach puts industrial-scale, meaningful quantum computing “years, not decades” away.
item.description: Captured at seed. No SymbiQ-tracked interim milestone yet -- see sourcing_note for the reason this claimant specifically needs independent replication, not just a press release, before any check-in here is marked on_track.

item.title: Check-in (on track): Quantinuum will deliver universal, fully fault-tolerant quantum computing (system “Apollo”) by 2030.
item.description: Interim milestone Helios (≈100 physical qubits, two-qubit gate error <5×10⁻⁴) launched commercially per Quantinuum's Nov 2025 announcements, one step on the path to Apollo -- named here as the check-in to track, not as evidence the 2030 claim itself has resolved.

item.title: Check-in (no signal): Rigetti's own roadmap commits to a 100+ qubit chiplet system in 2025, 150+ qubits in 2026, and 1,000+ qubits in 2027.
item.description: Captured at seed. Worth noting for context: Rigetti's public roadmap has moved before -- an earlier iteration of this same roadmap targeted 100+ qubits with 99.5% median two-qubit fidelity specifically "by the end of 2025," reported the same week -- so the 2025 leg of this claim is the nearest-term thing to watch first.

item.title: Now tracking: Atom Computing and Microsoft announced a commercial quantum machine with 24 entangled logical qubits, available for delivery in 2025.
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-08-27. Resolves by 2025-12-31 (+30 day grace). Criteria: Resolves VERIFIED if a commercial customer actually received and operated a system matching the 24-entangled-logical-qubit specification by 31 Dec 2025 (plus grace) -- an order or a demo does not count, an operating delivered system does. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if a related but differently-specified system shipped in the window (e.g. a different logical-qubit count) instead of the exact one announced. NOT_VERIFIED if no delivery happened in the stated window at all.

item.title: Now tracking: D-Wave says its Advantage2 annealing quantum computer demonstrated quantum computational supremacy on a real-world magnetic-materials simulation problem, beating classical supercomputers.
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-08-27. Resolves by 2026-12-31 (+30 day grace). Criteria: This is a claim about a result already published (Science, DOI 10.1126/science.ado6285, “Beyond-Classical Computation in Quantum Simulation”), not a future promise -- so what is being tracked is not whether it happens, but whether it HOLDS UP against classical rebuttals, which is exactly the kind of claim a credibility tracker exists for. Resolves VERIFIED if no classical algorithm has, by the resolution date, matched D-Wave's reported accuracy/runtime on the same problem instances at the same or larger scale. NOT_VERIFIED if a peer-reviewed classical method has matched or beaten it at comparable scale. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if classical methods match it at smaller scales tested so far (as the two rebuttals below currently claim) but have not yet been shown to scale to D-Wave's largest reported instances.

item.title: Now tracking: Executive Order 14412 requires U.S. federal high-value assets to migrate to post-quantum key establishment by 31 December 2030, and to post-quantum digital signatures by 31 December 2031.
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-08-27. Resolves by 2030-12-31 (+30 day grace). Criteria: Resolves VERIFIED if OMB and covered federal agencies report, by 31 Dec 2030 (plus grace), that high-value-asset and high-impact systems (excluding National Security Systems, which run on the separate CNSA 2.0 timeline) have completed PQC key-establishment migration per Section 4(b)(ii). The Dec 2031 digital-signature deadline is a distinct, secondary check-in, not the primary resolution date. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if key establishment is done but materially behind on signatures past their own deadline. NOT_VERIFIED if the 2030 date is missed outright, superseded if a later executive action changes the deadline before then (log as a revision, not a quiet edit).

item.title: Now tracking: Google has set 2029 as its internal deadline to complete post-quantum cryptography migration across its infrastructure.
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-08-27. Resolves by 2029-12-31 (+30 day grace). Criteria: Resolves VERIFIED if Google publicly states, by 31 Dec 2029 (plus grace), that its own infrastructure's post-quantum cryptography migration is complete, consistent with the phased plan in the same post (store-now-decrypt-later priority items by end of 2027). PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if the store-now-decrypt-later-priority subset is done but the full migration is not. NOT_VERIFIED if neither has happened by the deadline plus grace.

item.title: Now tracking: NVIDIA's Jensen Huang said truly useful quantum computers are 15 to 30 years away, with 20 years as the figure “a whole bunch of us would believe.”
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-08-27. Resolves by 2040-01-06 (+30 day grace). Criteria: A genuinely hedged range, not a point claim, so it is tracked at both ends rather than forced into one deadline. EARLY-END check (this claim's primary resolves_by, 15 years out): if a quantum computer has, by 6 Jan 2040, solved a problem of real commercial or scientific value faster or cheaper than the best available classical alternative -- independently verified, not a vendor's own benchmark -- that falsifies even Huang's optimistic bound (NOT_VERIFIED: he was wrong on the early side too). If no such result exists by then, log a check-in and continue tracking toward the LATE-END gate, 6 Jan 2055 (30 years): if by then still no such result exists, that falsifies the claim from the other direction (NOT_VERIFIED: even the generous bound was too generous). VERIFIED only if the first genuine instance lands inside the window itself, closest to the ~20-year midpoint he named as the figure most people in the field would actually believe.

item.title: Now tracking: IBM will deliver a large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computer (“Starling”) by 2029, running 100 million quantum operations on 200 logical qubits.
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-08-27. Resolves by 2029-12-31 (+30 day grace). Criteria: Resolves VERIFIED if IBM has, by 31 Dec 2029, publicly demonstrated a machine matching the Starling specification (fault-tolerant, ~200 logical qubits, capable of on the order of 100 million quantum operations) -- an IBM announcement plus independent technical reporting confirming the specification counts. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if a materially smaller or delayed system ships under the Starling name. NOT_VERIFIED if no fault-tolerant system in this class has shipped by the deadline plus the 30-day grace period.

item.title: Now tracking: IonQ targeted 99.999% (“five nines”) logical two-qubit gate fidelity by the end of 2025.
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-08-27. Resolves by 2025-12-31 (+30 day grace). Criteria: Resolves VERIFIED if IonQ published, by 31 Dec 2025 (plus the 30-day grace period, i.e. by 30 Jan 2026), an independently reportable result of >=99.999% logical two-qubit gate fidelity using small-distance QEC codes, matching this specific figure -- not to be conflated with the same announcement's separate >99.9% NATIVE two-qubit gate fidelity target, a different and less stringent number. NOT_VERIFIED if no such result was published. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if a result close to but short of five nines (e.g. four nines) was published and reported as the headline achievement instead.

item.title: Now tracking: Microsoft says its Majorana 1 / Topological Core approach puts industrial-scale, meaningful quantum computing “years, not decades” away.
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-08-27. Resolves by 2035-02-19 (+30 day grace). Criteria: This claim names no specific year -- “years, not decades” is a hedge, not a deadline, so it fails intake rule 4 (deadlined) as stated. SymbiQ's own falsifiability construction, flagged as such rather than attributed to Microsoft: resolves NOT_VERIFIED if, by 19 Feb 2035 (ten years from the claim, the outer edge of what “years, not decades” can plausibly mean before it is simply wrong), no topological-qubit system from Microsoft has demonstrated a problem of genuine industrial scale and consequence that a classical computer could not also solve. VERIFIED if one has. This is deliberately a lenient, favourable-to-the-claimant reading of a vague sentence.

item.title: Now tracking: Quantinuum will deliver universal, fully fault-tolerant quantum computing (system “Apollo”) by 2030.
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-08-27. Resolves by 2030-12-31 (+30 day grace). Criteria: Resolves VERIFIED if Quantinuum has, by 31 Dec 2030, shipped or publicly operated a system matching the Apollo specification (universal, fully fault-tolerant, circuits of millions of gates) -- confirmed by a Quantinuum announcement plus independent technical reporting. Note the press release's own text separately targets Apollo itself for 2029, one year ahead of the “by 2030” headline claim; both dates are logged so either can be checked against what actually ships. PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if an earlier-generation system (Helios, Sol) ships on schedule but Apollo itself is delayed past 2030. NOT_VERIFIED otherwise.

item.title: Now tracking: Rigetti's own roadmap commits to a 100+ qubit chiplet system in 2025, 150+ qubits in 2026, and 1,000+ qubits in 2027.
item.description: Claim captured and its resolution criteria frozen on 2026-08-27. Resolves by 2027-12-31 (+30 day grace). Criteria: Resolves VERIFIED if Rigetti has, by 31 Dec 2027 (plus grace), shipped or operated a system matching each named year's qubit-count target within that year -- checked against Rigetti's own quarterly technical updates and independent reporting, not press-release qubit counts alone (this project's own recurring lesson: a qubit count without connectivity/fidelity context is close to meaningless -- see race.html). PARTIALLY_VERIFIED if the 2025/2026 interim targets slip but the 2027 endpoint is still substantially met. NOT_VERIFIED if the 2027 target is missed outright.

item.title: Check-in (at risk): D-Wave says its Advantage2 annealing quantum computer demonstrated quantum computational supremacy on a real-world magnetic-materials simulation problem, beating classical supercomputers.
item.description: Linda Mauron and Giuseppe Carleo (EPFL) posted a separate classical approach (time-dependent variational Monte Carlo) to arXiv, reporting correlation errors below 7% on systems up to 128 spins -- “aligning with or surpassing” D-Wave's reported accuracy at that scale, though not yet tested at D-Wave's largest reported instances.

item.title: Check-in (at risk): D-Wave says its Advantage2 annealing quantum computer demonstrated quantum computational supremacy on a real-world magnetic-materials simulation problem, beating classical supercomputers.
item.description: Flatiron Institute (Joseph Tindall et al.) posted a classical belief-propagation approach to arXiv claiming it “demonstrably outperforms other reported methods” on the same spin-glass problem, with errors “noticeably lower than the quantum annealing approach” -- not yet peer-reviewed at time of posting.
